title: Open immersions from spaces descend under fpqc scheme covers
statement: Let $S,P$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $Z$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $a:Z\to P$ be an $S$-morphism. Let $\{P_i\to P\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering by schemes [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Suppose each $Z_i=Z\times_PP_i$ is a scheme and the projection $a_i:Z_i\to P_i$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $a$ identifies $Z$ with an open subscheme of $P$. In particular $Z$ is a scheme and $a$ is an open immersion. No representability or quasi-compactness assumption on $a$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 041X (lemma-descending-property-open-immersion), descent implication for algebraic-space source and scheme target; an open subspace of a scheme is a scheme.

proof.text: For local presentations k_i:h_X_i→Z and q_i:X_i→P_i, the square (k_i,q_i,a,p_i) is cartesian, by transporting the given pullback isomorphism. On a double overlap T with projections b:T→P_i and c:T→P_j, pull back q_i along b. Its universal section of Z and map to P_j lift uniquely through the cartesian presentation X_j. The equality of their composites to P_j shows that the inverse image of the image of q_i is contained in that of q_j. Interchanging i and j gives equality of the opens. This uses only the scheme and presheaf pullback universal properties, rather than a separately stated open-immersion base-change theorem.

source.place: Tag 041X (lemma-descending-property-open-immersion), equality of the two inverse-image opens; scheme base change Tag 01JY

proof.text: Apply descent of compatible open subschemes to $\{P_i\to P\}$ and the opens of step 1. Obtain an open subscheme $U\subset P$ with $P_i\times_PU=U_i$ for every $i$. Write $j:U\hookrightarrow P$ for its inclusion. This application uses the full covering-family form of descent, so no reduction to a quasi-compact singleton cover is needed.

source.place: Tag 041X (lemma-descending-property-open-immersion), descent of the image open by Descent Tag 03N0 (lemma-open-fpqc-covering)

proof.text: For any $S$-scheme $T$ and $z\in Z(T)$, let $f=a(z):T\to P$ and $T_i=T\times_PP_i$. The family $\{T_i\to T\}$ is fpqc, hence jointly surjective. The section $z|_{T_i}$ together with $T_i\to P_i$ gives a point of $Z_i(T_i)$, so the latter map factors through $U_i$. Consequently $f(T)\subset U$: for $t\in T$ choose a point over $t$ in some $T_i$, whose image in $P_i$ belongs to $U_i=P_i\times_PU$. Open factorization gives a unique $b_T(z):T\to U$ with $j b_T(z)=f$. For any $k:T'\to T$, both $b_T(z)k$ and $b_{T'}(z|_{T'})$ have composite $fk$ with $j$, so uniqueness makes them equal. Thus $b:Z\to h_U$ is a natural transformation over $h_P$, where $h_U(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,U)$.

source.place: Tag 041X (lemma-descending-property-open-immersion), final test-scheme factorization argument; Topologies Tag 022D and Schemes Tag 01HI

proof.text: First show a is injective on sections: if two sections on T have the same image f:T→P, pull back the fpqc cover by f. The cartesian presentation X_i supplies lifts of both sections with the same map to P_i; monicity of q_i makes these lifts equal. Fpqc sheaf uniqueness for Z gives equality on T. Conversely, for f:T→P whose image lies in the descended open U, pull back the fpqc family to T_i=T×_P P_i. The map T_i→P_i has image in q_i(X_i), since p_i^{-1}(U)=q_i(X_i), and thus factors uniquely through q_i. Composing with k_i gives sections of Z over T_i. Their images under a are f restricted to T_i, so the injectivity just proved makes them agree on every overlap. Apply fpqc sheaf gluing for Z. Naturality of a and the separated fpqc sheaf property of the representable presheaf h_P show that the glued section has image f.

source.place: Tag 041X (lemma-descending-property-open-immersion), fpqc gluing and the final bijection; Tag 04P2 (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), Properties of Spaces Tag 0APL, Descent Tag 023Q

proof.text: The unique open factorizations from step 3 form a natural transformation b:Z→h_U: restriction commutes with factorization by monicity of U→P. Its component at each T is injective by the first part of step 4, and surjective by applying the second part to the composite of any T→U with U→P. Therefore each component is an isomorphism of types, hence b is a presheaf isomorphism. Its composite with the Yoneda image of the open inclusion is a, by the open-factorization equation.

source.place: Tag 041X (lemma-descending-property-open-immersion), concluding bijection of sheaves with the open subscheme
